title: Power-of-two small-bias parameters
statement: Let $d$ and $b$ be integers with $d>0$ and $0\le b\le d$, and set $n=2^{d-b}$ and $\varepsilon=2^{-b}$. Choose $r,s$ independently and uniformly from the binary extension field of degree $d$, and form a binary vector of length $n$ whose coordinate indexed by $i$ is the dot product over $\mathbb F_2$ of the basis-coordinate vectors of $r^{i+1}$ and $s$. The output distribution, viewed as a density relative to the uniform distribution on the binary cube, has every nonzero Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\varepsilon$; moreover, the multiset of outputs as $(r,s)$ ranges over all field pairs has cardinality at most $16(n/\varepsilon)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: The field degree d is positive
The integer b satisfies 0 ≤ b ≤ d
